package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, triggering data theft as soon as the package is installed.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious.example.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrate credential files to attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to user's private keys and cloud credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of code in setup.py that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during installation.
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious.example.com/upload initiated from setup.py.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations where setup.py reads sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to external domains, specifically https://malicious.example.com/upload. Flag any package whose setup.py contains code that accesses these files or performs network exfiltration during installation.
